newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-UGLY DUCKLINGS WIN LIBERTADORES CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UGLY DUCKLINGS WIN LIBERTADORES CUP.

text.p: Cruzeiro's Libertadores Cup triumph was a blow to the mainstream of Brazilian soccer.

The club, from the country's third largest city of Belo Horizonte, have been looked down on by the Brazilian soccer establishment for years simply because they do not come from either Rio de Janeiro or Sao Paulo.

Cruzeiro players rarely make the national team and their campaign in this year's Libertadores, South America's top club competition, was almost completely ignored in the two cities that consider themselves the country's main soccer centres.

Incredibly, Brazilian soccer fans were not able to watch Cruzeiro's games on television, the country's networks preferring to show run-of-the-mill Brazilian championship games involving teams from Rio or Sao Paulo.
One station finally relented on Wednesday for the second leg of the final and decided Cruzeiro were worthy of national viewing.
Despite this, the club, considered the rich cousins in a city where the masses prefer Atletico Mineiro, are one of Brazil's most successful at international level.

Cruzeiro, who beat Peru's Sporting Cristal 1-0 on Wednesday to win the final 1-0 on aggregate, have won the Libertadores Cup twice, the South American Supercup twice and reached the final of each tournament on a further occasion.
The four major Rio de Janeiro clubs, on the other hand, have managed one Libertadores title between them, when Flamengo lifted the trophy in 1981.
Corinthians, the best supported club in Sao Paulo, have never won an international title, nor have Palmeiras, the city's second most popular team.

When Gremio, from the southern Brazilian city of Porto Alegre, won the Libertadores two years ago, coach Luis Felipe Scolari complained bitterly that his side were not given the recognition they deserved.
The team were continually criticised for being over- physical, and Scolari insisted his side were being victimised by Sao Paulo media.

Gremio followed their Libertadores triumph by winning the 1996 Brazilian championship, yet in those two years their only reward at national team level was two caps in low-key friendlies for goalkeeper Danrlei.
Midfielder Dinho, considered the most physical of Gremio's players, was picked by the national team in 1993 -- but he played for Sao Paulo at the time.
Many players, however, seem happier at clubs such as Cruzeiro, where the fans are less demanding and mistakes are tolerted.
Cruzeiro central defender Gelson joined the club after being hounded outof Flamengo by impatient fans after just a couple of poor performances bad game.
Other players such as right-back Vitor, captain Wilson Gottardo, strikers Palhinha and Elivelton and midfielder Fabinho all came to Cruzeiro after unhappy experiences in Rio and Sao Paulo.
Yet Cruzeiro are still regarded as poor relations, ignored when the major clubs from Rio and Sao Paulo organised a pre-season tournament and liable to have their top players poached at any moment.
On Thursday, coach Paulo Autuori was already packing his bags after being offered a new job, by struggling Rio de Janeiro giants Flamengo.
